title: Movie Collection
story: Your movie collection has grown to hundreds of titles. You want to tag each one with a genre and quickly find the classics. An enum for genre and a bool-returning function make this trivial.
why: Enums turn vague categories into compile-time-checked labels � no typos like "Sci-Fi" vs "SciFi".
analogy: An enum is like a dropdown menu on a streaming site � you can only pick from the listed genres. A free-text field would let you type "Comdy" by mistake.
try_it: Add more genres (Romance, Documentary, Animation). Create a small collection of 5 movies across different genres and write a function that returns the most common genre in your collection.
tips: Enum variants are accessed with `TypeName.Variant` � like `Genre.SciFi`
Use `==` to compare enum values (the variants themselves must be comparable)
Think of enums as a fixed vocabulary � the compiler is your spellchecker
common_mistakes: Typing `SciFi` directly instead of `Genre.SciFi` � the compiler needs the type prefix
Comparing enum values from different enum types (e.g., `Genre.Action == Mood.Happy`) � impossible
